title: LATTE: A Framework for Learning Item-Features to Make a Domain-Expert for Effective Conversational Recommendation

problem.claim: Conversational recommender systems need to recommend suitable items by capturing item features mentioned in dialogue and explain relevant features of recommended items.

contributions.claim: LATTE pre-trains the recommendation and conversation modules of a conversational recommender system using external data.
The recommendation module uses multi-reviews and a knowledge graph to learn relationships between items and their features.
The conversation module uses synthetic dialogues with feature-based explanations generated from item features and dialogue templates.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe LATTE as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On two public conversational recommendation datasets, the authors report effectiveness of each LATTE module.
The authors report superiority over seven state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report interpretations based on visualization.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality conversational recommendation requires feature-aware recommendation and explanation.
The CRS model should act as a domain expert knowledgeable about item-feature relationships and context-relevant explanations.
LATTE pre-trains recommendation and conversation modules using external data, multi-reviews, a knowledge graph, synthetic dialogues, and templates.
Experiments on two public datasets report module effectiveness, superiority over seven state-of-the-art methods, and visualization-based interpretations.

source_observation.claim: LATTE pre-trains separate recommendation and conversation modules with different external-data strategies.

interpretation.claim: Module-specific pre-training can align learning signals with distinct recommendation and explanation responsibilities.

application.claim: For a conversational recommendation system, consider combining structured item-feature learning with synthetic explanation-oriented dialogue pre-training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the two public datasets evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, evaluation metrics, or experimental results.
The abstract does not identify the seven comparison methods.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, or reproducibility information.
